title: Data Attribute Selectors
definition: Using the `data-*` variant to style elements based on custom HTML data attributes.
simpleExplanation: A modern alternative to `peer` and `group` classes. In React, you dynamically apply `data-state="open"` to a dropdown menu. You can then use Tailwind's `data-[state=open]:opacity-100` to style it. This creates an incredibly clean separation between JavaScript logic and CSS styling.
realWorldExample: The Radix UI library exclusively uses `data-state` attributes to tell the DOM what is happening. Tailwind perfectly intercepts these attributes to apply styles.

basic: What Tailwind variant allows you to style an element when it has `data-active="true"` in its HTML?
intermediate: Why is styling based on `data-*` attributes often preferred over toggling an `.is-active` CSS class?

answers.question: Why preferred over classes?
answers.answer: Because `data-*` attributes can hold string values (`data-state="loading"`, `data-state="success"`), making them much more expressive and readable than having a mess of separate classes like `.is-loading` and `.is-success`.
